dicas.texto: Você está no caminho certo! Se cada copo inteiro tem 4 partes de um quarto, quantas partes de um quarto existem em 2 copos inteiros?
Tente multiplicar a parte inteira (2) pelo denominador (4) e depois somar com o numerador da fração (3) para encontrar o total de quartos.
Você tem 8 quartos nos dois copos inteiros. Agora, adicione os 3 quartos que sobraram. Qual o total de quartos?
Você tem 8/4 + 3/4. Somando os numeradores, você chega no valor final que deve colocar na caixa de cima, mantendo o denominador 4 embaixo.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 4 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: Focus first on the cups that were completely filled, before considering the leftover part.
Separate the amount into complete cups and the fractional part of another cup.
Count the two cups that were filled completely.
Enter the number of complete cups in the m1 field.
A mixed number shows a whole-number part together with a fractional part.
Use the conversion control after identifying the complete cups and the leftover fraction.
Find the button labeled ... below or beside the fraction fields.
Press ... once so the fields for the mixed number become available.
The numerator counts how many equal fractional parts make up the entire amount.
Multiply the whole-number part by the denominator, then add the numerator of the fractional part.
Represent each complete cup as four fourths, then include the three additional fourths.
Perform the multiplication of the whole part by the denominator and add the fractional numerator before entering the result in f1.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.
When converting a mixed number to an improper fraction, keep the denominator of the original fractional part.
Look at the number below the bar in the fractional part of the mixed number.
Copy the fractional denominator into the lower field, f2.
Locate the point by considering both the two complete units and the remaining fractional part.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the position represented by the improper fraction.
The point must be between 2 and 3, three of the four equal intervals after 2.
Start at 2 and move three quarter-intervals toward 3, then place the point there.
Before finishing, make sure the marked point represents the total amount of juice.
Check the fraction fields and compare the point with the four-part intervals on the number line.
Confirm that the point is between 2 and 3 and lies three quarter-intervals after 2.
When the fraction fields and the point are checked, press the button labeled ....

exercicio.statement:
Every morning, Lili's mother prepares a pitcher of tomato juice for Lili and her sister. One morning, Lili's mother made the pitcher a bit too large; it completely filled Lili's cup, her sister's up, and the left over filled about 3/4 of a third cup. Show the number of cups of tomato juice Lili's mother prepared that morning on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?

steps.instruction: In m1, enter the whole-number part of the amount of juice.
Click Convert to open the mixed-number fields and represent the quantity as a mixed number.
In f1, enter the numerator of the improper fraction.
In f2, enter the denominator of the improper fraction.
Mark 11/4 on the number line from 0 to 3.
After checking the point, click Done to finish the problem.
